data.name: Bhanavi
data.gender_notes: Bhanavi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhanu means 'sun' and vi means 'knowledge'. This name signifies the goddess of knowledge and wisdom, Bhanu-vi. In Hindu mythology, Bhanu is one of the twenty-seven stars (Nakshatras) and is associated with the sun. The name Bhanavi carries the meaning “Goddess of knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhanavi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bhanavi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhanavi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

It also reflects the importance of knowledge and wisdom, which has been a significant aspect of Indian culture for centuries. This name can be seen as a sun of knowledge, radiant and powerful.
data.spiritual_significance: This name carries the blessings of the Hindu goddess of knowledge and wisdom, Saraswati, who is often depicted holding a veena (an ancient instrument) and a book, symbolizing art and knowledge. Bhanavi is believed to imbibe the spiritual traits of this goddess, making it a meaningful and significant name for a child. historical_references.reference: Bhanavi was an influential Jaina saint from 9th century Karnataka. She is regarded as the founder of the Bhanati sub-sect of the Digambara Jains.
Bhanavi was a royal queen of the Chalukya dynasty in 11th century Andhra Pradesh. She is known for her deep devotion to Lord Vishnu and is believed to have built several temples dedicated to him.

trends: Bhanavi is a popular name among Hindu communities, particularly in India and Nepal. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'bhana' meaning 'to build' or 'to create'. In modern times, this name has become more popular due to its unique sound and meaning.
